title: Riemann Zeta Function
subtitle: Special Functions · Analytic number theory
summary: Fundamental in analytic number theory. Its non-trivial zeros are the subject of the Riemann Hypothesis.
detail:
\[ \zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^s} = \prod_p \frac{1}{1-p^{-s}} \]

Analytically continued to \(\mathbb{C}\setminus\{1\}\). Special values: \(\zeta(2)=\pi^2/6\), \(\zeta(4)=\pi^4/90\). The Riemann Hypothesis asserts all non-trivial zeros lie on \(\operatorname{Re}(s)=1/2\). The functional equation relates \(\zeta(s)\) to \(\zeta(1-s)\).
